# T9 — Template tab + live PDF preview

## What was built

The live PDF preview pane (mounted once, visible on both tabs) and the real Template tab body,
replacing T8's two placeholder seams. Both talk to `POST /api/resumes/:id/render` only — never
`/pdf`, which persists a snapshot.

### Files added

- `components/editor/PreviewPane.tsx` — replaces `PreviewPanePlaceholder.tsx`. Owns a debounced
  (600ms), coalescing render queue built on `createAutosave` (reused exactly as `t8-seams.md`
  suggested — it already guarantees "never two in flight, always converge on the latest scheduled
  state" for free), the page-count badge (prominent amber styling once `pages > 1`), the
  errors panel (LaTeX compile failures), and the warnings panel (dangling ids / empty sections),
  and keeps the last successfully-rendered PDF on screen under a failed render rather than
  blanking it.
- `components/editor/PdfViewer.tsx` — the actual `react-pdf` `<Document>`/`<Page>` wrapper. Only
  ever loaded client-side (see the react-pdf section below).
- `components/editor/TemplateTab.tsx` — replaces `TemplateTabPlaceholder.tsx`. The
  `GlobalEditBadge`-flagged header, the four-token legend with click-to-insert-at-cursor buttons,
  and the LaTeX editor.
- `components/editor/TemplateEditor.tsx` — the `<textarea>`-based LaTeX editor: monospace, a
  synced line-number gutter, and Tab-key handling that inserts a literal tab instead of moving
  focus. Deliberately not CodeMirror/Monaco per the task brief.
- `lib/preview/pdf-blob.ts` + `.test.ts` — the one pure helper extracted from the fetch/render
  flow: `base64PdfToObjectUrl`, decoding the render endpoint's base64 PDF into a `blob:` URL.
  1 `node:test` case (round-trips arbitrary bytes through `Buffer`/`atob`/`Blob`/`fetch`).
- `public/pdf.worker.min.mjs` — a static copy of `node_modules/pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.worker.min.mjs`
  (react-pdf's own resolved `pdfjs-dist` version, currently 5.4.296), served locally so the
  worker is never fetched from a CDN that could drift out of version-lock with the bundled
  `pdfjs-dist`. Not part of any build step — copied once by hand; see Gaps below.

### Files extended

- `lib/api-client.ts` — added `renderResume(id, templateOverride?)`, following the exact
  `requestJson` pattern every other function uses. A LaTeX compile failure is `200 { ok: false,
  errors, warnings }`, never a thrown `ApiError` (same shape as `saveResumePdf`, per
  `docs/agents/t6.md` Deviations #2) — `PreviewPane` checks `.ok`, it never relies on a `catch`
  for compile errors.
- `components/editor/ResumeEditor.tsx` — minimal, surgical edits per the seams doc:
  - Swapped the two placeholder imports/usages for `PreviewPane`/`TemplateTab`.
  - Added one new handler, `onTemplateContentChange`, following the exact same pattern as every
    other content-field handler already in the file (`onExperienceFieldChange` etc.): optimistic
    local `setState` update + `autosave.getController('template:content', ..., 1000).schedule(...)`.
  - **No separate `draftTemplateContent` state was added.** `t8-seams.md` suggested lifting one;
    I used `state.template.content` itself as the live draft instead (same as how every other
    content field already works — the in-memory value *is* the draft, autosave persists it in the
    background). This is one field-diff from the seams doc, not an extra one, and keeps
    `PreviewPane` always in sync with whatever's in the editor with no separate variable to drift
    out of sync. See Deviations.
  - `PreviewPane` receives `templateContent={state.template.content}` (always sent as
    `templateOverride`, whether or not it differs from what's actually persisted — the preview is
    of what's on screen, per the task brief),  `selections`, and `library` (the latter two are
    only used as change-detection signals inside `PreviewPane`, not sent over the wire — `render`
    always re-reads persisted selections/content from the database itself; see Deviations).
- `next.config.ts` — two `webpack.resolve.alias` entries required to make `react-pdf` work at all
  under Next; see below.

## The react-pdf approach, and the dev-mode trap I actually hit

I used `react-pdf` + `pdfjs-dist` as instructed, not the iframe fallback — it works, including
under `next dev`, but getting there required two `next.config.ts` aliases, one of which was not
the one the task brief warned about:

1. **`canvas: false`** — the documented trap. `pdfjs-dist` has a guarded, Node-only `require('canvas')`
   fallback path that webpack still tries to resolve for the client bundle unless aliased away.
2. **`'pdfjs-dist$': require.resolve('pdfjs-dist/build/pdf.min.mjs')`** — not documented in the
   task brief, and not the CDN/worker-version-mismatch trap it warned about (I did avoid that one:
   the worker is a locally-served static file, matched by construction since it's copied from the
   same `node_modules/pdfjs-dist` react-pdf itself resolves — never a CDN). This one is a
   **`next dev` (webpack) + `pdfjs-dist`'s unminified `build/pdf.mjs` bundle interaction bug**:
   loading the dynamically-imported `PdfViewer` chunk crashed on mount with
   `TypeError: Object.defineProperty called on non-object`, thrown from webpack's own
   `__webpack_require__.r()` ES-module marker while evaluating `pdf.mjs`'s dev-mode
   eval-wrapped source — before any of my code runs at all. `npm run build && npm run start`
   (production) never hit this; only `next dev`'s webpack pipeline did. Aliasing `pdfjs-dist` to
   its own pre-minified build (`pdf.min.mjs` — same version, same API, just not the multi-thousand-
   line unminified source that appears to trip whatever dev-mode source transform is involved)
   made it disappear in both dev and prod, with no behavior change (confirmed via the manual
   verification below, including the compile-failure/recovery cycle, in a real `next dev` session).
   I did not root-cause the exact webpack/Next internals further than that — flagging here in case
   a `pdfjs-dist` version bump reintroduces it.
3. `next/dynamic({ ssr: false })` for `PdfViewer` (react-pdf touches canvas/DOM APIs that don't
   exist server-side) — the other documented trap, handled as instructed.

I did **not** need the iframe/blob-URL fallback. react-pdf works correctly in both `next dev` and
`next build && next start` once the two aliases above are in place.

## Debounce / coalescing design (requirement 2)

`PreviewPane` schedules a render via one `createAutosave<{ templateContent: string }>({ debounceMs:
600, save })` controller, created once via a lazy `useRef`. A `useEffect` calls `.schedule(...)`
whenever `selections`, `library`, or `templateContent` change (the first two are only
JSON-stringified as a change signal — `render` itself always re-reads the resume's persisted
selections/content from the database; only `templateContent` is actually sent, as
`templateOverride`). `createAutosave`'s existing coalescing (documented in `lib/editor/autosave.ts`
and exercised by `lib/editor/autosave.test.ts`) is exactly the "never two in flight, always
converge on the latest state" behavior the task asked for — I didn't need to write new coalescing
logic, just reuse it with a payload type shaped for rendering instead of saving.

One inherent limitation this reuse doesn't fully paper over: `render` reads *persisted* content
from the database, not whatever's in `library`/`selections` client state at the instant of the
call. Selection toggles are already saved immediately (debounce 0) so they're essentially always
current by the time the 600ms render debounce fires. Text-field edits (bullets, experience/project
fields) save on their own 500ms debounce; since both timers start from the same keystroke and the
render debounce is 100ms longer, in practice the content PATCH has almost always landed and
completed by the time the render request goes out — but this is a timing coincidence, not a
guarantee (a slow network could show the preview one keystroke-burst behind, self-correcting on
the very next render). Fixing this properly would mean `render` accepting a content override the
way it already accepts `templateOverride`, which is outside this task's file ownership.

## Keeping the last-good PDF visible on compile failure (requirement 3)

`PreviewPane` tracks the last successful render (`{ fileUrl, pages }`) completely separately from
the current errors/warnings. A failed render (`ok: false`) only ever updates `errors`/`warnings` —
the `good` state (and the `<PdfViewer>` it feeds) is untouched, so a transient LaTeX error while
typing shows the error panel *above* the still-rendered last-good PDF rather than blanking it.
Verified end-to-end manually (see below): breaking the template, confirming the error panel +
retained page count, then fixing it and confirming the error clears and the preview updates again.

### `POST /render` shape, verified directly with curl

```
$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/resumes/$ID/render -H "x-resumix-token: $TOKEN" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{}'
{"ok":true,"pages":1,"errors":[],"warnings":[],"pdfBase64":"..."}   # (125460 chars of base64)

$ curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/resumes/$ID/render -H "x-resumix-token: $TOKEN" \
    -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -d '{"templateOverride":"\\documentclass{article}\n\\begin{document}\n\\badcommandthatdoesnotexist{oops}\n<<EXPERIENCES>>\n\\end{document}"}' \
    -w "\nHTTP_STATUS:%{http_code}\n"
{"ok":false,"pages":null,"errors":["./resume.tex:3: Undefined control sequence. (l.3 \\badcommandthatdoesnotexist)","./resume.tex:3:  ==> Fatal error occurred, no output PDF file produced!"],"warnings":[],"log":"..."}
HTTP_STATUS:200
```

Confirms exactly the `200 { ok: false, errors, warnings }` shape `PreviewPane.tsx`'s error-handling
branch depends on — never a thrown/caught HTTP error for a compile failure.

### Manual, real-browser verification (`npm run dev`, real Postgres + real latex sidecar)

I do not have a GUI to look at directly in this environment, so I used the `playwright` package
already present in the shared `node_modules` (not a project dependency — used only as an ad hoc
verification tool, not added to `package.json`) to drive a real headless Chromium against the
running `next dev` server, seed `localStorage` with a real auth token, and both read the DOM and
take screenshots. I looked at every screenshot before writing this report.

- **SSR sanity**: `curl` of `/resume/:id` returns `200` with no error text in the HTML (this only
  confirms the RSC shell renders without a server-side exception — `AuthGate` itself only resolves
  client-side from `localStorage`, so the substantive check is the headless-browser one below).
- **First real render, Content tab**: navigated with the token pre-seeded, waited for the debounced
  first render. Result: **zero console/page errors**, page count reads "1 page", and the rendered
  PDF visually matches the seeded default resume (screenshot showed the full Chris Pyle resume,
  correctly laid out). This is the same page that crashed with `Object.defineProperty called on
  non-object` before the `pdfjs-dist` alias fix above — I saw that crash first, root-caused it, and
  then confirmed it gone, all in this same session.
- **Template tab**: clicked the tab, screenshot shows the global-edit badge, the four `<<TOKEN>>`
  legend buttons, line-numbered LaTeX, and the same live PDF still visible on the right.
- **Compile-failure → recovery cycle**: typed `\badcommandxyz{oops}` at the top of the template via
  real keyboard input, waited for the debounce: error panel appeared
  ("The template failed to compile — showing the last good preview.") with the actual LaTeX log
  line, **and the last-good PDF and its "1 page" badge stayed on screen**, confirmed via
  screenshot. Then restored the original template text: error panel cleared, "1 page" still shown,
  confirmed via a second screenshot and a body-text assertion (`failed to compile` no longer
  present).
- **Debounce/coalescing against real network traffic**: toggled an experience's selection checkbox
  on the Content tab and captured the actual requests fired: exactly one
  `PUT .../selections` (immediate, per T8's existing selection autosave) followed by exactly one
  `POST .../render` — not two, not zero — confirming the 600ms debounce fires once per settled
  change rather than once per keystroke/click.
- Re-seeded the database (`--force`) after this session to leave the shared dev database clean —
  my test script briefly PATCHed the real seeded template with malformed LaTeX while iterating on
  the recovery-cycle test (an artifact of an earlier, buggy version of the test script actually
  exercising the real global-autosave-to-`/api/templates/:id` path, exactly as designed — global
  template edits really do persist for every resume, which is the point, but not something I
  wanted to leave in the shared dev DB).

### What I did **not** verify

- No visual check of the resizable split-pane divider interacting with `PdfViewer`'s
  `ResizeObserver`-driven page width while dragging (I didn't script a drag gesture in headless
  Chromium) — the resize wiring itself is unchanged from T8, and `PdfViewer` re-measures on any
  container resize, but I only confirmed the initial-width case by screenshot, not the live-drag
  case.
- No check of a resume that actually spans >1 pages (the seeded default resume is 1 page), so the
  amber "⚠ N pages" styling was checked by code review and a light DOM-class check, not by seeing
  it rendered against real multi-page content.
- No automated (`node:test`) coverage of `PreviewPane`/`TemplateTab`/`PdfViewer` themselves — like
  T8's Content-tab components, these are React components wired to the network and DOM, outside
  this project's plain `node:test` (no jsdom/RTL) setup; covered instead by the pure-logic test
  (`pdf-blob.test.ts`) and the manual browser session above.

## Deviations from a literal reading of the brief / the seams doc

- **No separate `draftTemplateContent` state.** `t8-seams.md` suggested lifting one into
  `ResumeEditor`; I used `state.template.content` as the draft directly (see above) — functionally
  equivalent, one fewer piece of state to keep in sync, and consistent with how every other
  content field in the file already works.
- **Template autosave debounce is 1000ms**, not the 500ms `t8-seams.md` suggested — the task brief
  given directly for this task explicitly says "~1s debounce" for `PATCH /api/templates/:id", and
  a full LaTeX document really is a much larger payload than a bullet, so I followed the more
  specific, more recent instruction.
- **Everything stayed under `components/editor/**`**, per `t8-seams.md`'s explicit "what NOT to
  touch" list, even though the top-level task instructions also permitted
  `components/preview/**`/`components/template/**`. I judged the seams doc's flat-import-graph
  rationale (matching T8's own file layout) more valuable than using the extra directories, given
  the two files this task added beyond the two replacements (`PdfViewer.tsx`, `TemplateEditor.tsx`)
  are small enough not to need their own subtree.
- **`next.config.ts` gained a `webpack` config block** — not called out in my file-ownership list,
  but unavoidable: without the `canvas`/`pdfjs-dist` aliases described above, react-pdf does not
  load in the browser at all, in dev or prod.
- **Reused T8's `SaveStatusBadge` component directly inside `TemplateTab`**, wired to the same
  aggregate `autosave.status`/`autosave.retryAll` already shown in the header, rather than building
  a new per-channel indicator — satisfies "reuse T8's autosave status indicator pattern" literally
  (same component, same semantics) without adding a second, possibly-inconsistent status source.

## Known gaps / left for follow-up

- The `render`-reads-from-database-not-from-client-state limitation described above (content edits
  can theoretically show one keystroke-burst stale in the preview under slow network conditions;
  self-corrects on the next render).
- `public/pdf.worker.min.mjs` is a hand-copied static asset, not produced by any build step or
  postinstall script — if `pdfjs-dist` is ever upgraded, this file needs to be re-copied by hand
  or a small `scripts/`/`package.json` step should be added to keep it in lock-step automatically.
- No multi-page resume was available to visually confirm the "⚠ N pages" amber treatment against
  real content (see "What I did not verify" above).
- `playwright` was used only as an ad hoc, uncommitted verification tool in this session (already
  present in the shared `node_modules`, not added to `package.json`) — there is still no actual
  browser-level automated test suite for this app; T8's gap here is unchanged.
